events.text:
## Recommendation

- **Go to South Haven's pier.** My expected rating is 2 (average), low confidence.
- **Rough pier ratings for this week:** South Haven 2, St. Joseph 2, Muskegon 2, Grand Haven 1.
- **Try the low light.** Fish early and late. Spoons and glow spoons are the lures that worked in low light.
- **Use spoons or meat rigs, and fish deep.** Boats found the fish 65 to 140 ft down, so a pier line that gets well below the surface is worth trying.

## Why

- South Haven had the most recent north-to-east wind (23 hours in the last 3 days), which should push cold water toward its pier.
- The South Haven boat report was slow (1, below average), so I'd expect the pier to be only average.
- Boats did best in the St. Joseph and Muskegon areas (quality 3), which is why those two are my close second choices.
- I'd expect low light to matter because the boat reports say glow spoons and low-light bites worked well.

## Evidence

**Recent reports (all salmon reports are boat reports, none from a pier):**
- Muskegon, 2026-08-03 (report dated 2022-08-03): boats found salmon 65 to 130 ft down in 140 to 250 ft of water; quality 3 (good); glow spoons, meat rigs and green or white flies all worked, and the bite was good in low light.
- St. Joseph, 2022-08-03: boats in 100+ ft of water; quality 3 (good); meat rigs and spoons caught most fish; fish moved in toward the end of the week.
- Grand Haven, 2022-08-03: boats in 120 to 220 ft of water, fish 65 to 140 ft down; quality 2 (average); green flies and meat rigs, with glow spoons in low light.
- South Haven, 2022-08-03: boats at about 100 ft; quality 1 (below average); a few Chinook and lake trout, mostly on spoons.
- Grand Haven and Muskegon, 2022-07-14: both slow (quality 0), with 54 to 58 hours of upwelling wind that week, which didn't produce a bite at the time.

**Past seasons (similar water temperature, within 14 days of today):**
- The only matching weeks are the 2022-08-03 reports above, so there is no separate history to add.

**Conditions now (the tool returned a summary for the week before 2022-08-09):**
- Surface water near the piers (satellite): St. Joseph 77 F, South Haven 76 F, Grand Haven 76 F, Muskegon 76 F; each was down about 1 F over the last 3 days.
- Upwelling wind over the last 3 days: South Haven 23 hours, St. Joseph 17, Grand Haven 13, Muskegon 12.
- Buoy surface water was about 76 F at all four ports, up 1 F over the week.
- Average wind that week was 7 to 10 mph, with gusts of 32 to 38 mph.

**General guidance (Michigan Sea Grant / MSU Extension):** mature Chinook in early fall hold in water of 55 F or less, and north or east winds bring cold water toward piers and river mouths.

## Caveats

- **Pier ratings are my estimates.** None of the reports covers pier fishing, and all the salmon data is boat-based.
- **The conditions data is not live.** The tool ran in backtest mode and gave a summary for the week before 2022-08-09. Check today's wind and forecast before you go.
- **The newest report is 6 days old (2022-08-03).** The fall season changes quickly, so treat it as a guide.
- **Depth may be out of reach from the pier.** The boat fish were 65 to 140 ft down, which a shore angler may not be able to reach.
- **Wind gusts** reached 32 to 38 mph that week. If the forecast is strong, the pier is risky. Check the forecast before you go.

## Sources

- https://content.govdelivery.com/accounts/MIDNR/bulletins/321350c (2022-07-14 bulletin: Grand Haven, Muskegon)
